questions.question_text: Identify the word that is most nearly opposite in meaning to 'Prudent'.
questions.explanation: Prudent implies acting with or showing care and thought for the future; reckless is the direct opposite.

questions.question_text: Choose the correct sentence: 'Neither the manager nor the employees ___ aware of the new policy.'
questions.explanation: In 'neither/nor' constructions, the verb agrees with the subject closest to it (employees), which is plural.
The correct spelling requires double 'c' and double 'm'.

questions.question_text: Which word is a synonym for 'Ephemeral'?
questions.explanation: Ephemeral means lasting for a very short time, which is synonymous with fleeting.

questions.question_text: Identify the part of speech for the word 'quickly' in the sentence: 'She ran quickly to the store.'
questions.explanation: Quickly modifies the verb 'ran', making it an adverb.

questions.question_text: Complete the sentence: 'The team ___ working on the project for weeks.'
questions.explanation: Team acts as a singular collective noun in this context, requiring 'has been'.

questions.question_text: Identify the sentence with the correct punctuation:
options: Its time to go, said John.
It's time to go, said John.
It is time to go; said John.
Its time to go - said John.
questions.explanation: It's is the contraction for 'it is', and the comma is used correctly to introduce speech.

options: Each of the students have finished the assignment.
Each of the students has finished the assignment.
Each of the students are finished the assignment.
Each of the students finish the assignment.
questions.explanation: 'Each' is a singular subject, requiring the singular verb 'has'.

questions.question_text: Which word is a synonym for 'Meticulous'?
questions.explanation: Meticulous means showing great attention to detail, which is synonymous with being thorough.

questions.question_text: Identify the gerund in the sentence: 'Running is his favorite hobby.'
questions.explanation: A gerund is a verb ending in -ing that functions as a noun. Here, 'Running' is the subject.

questions.question_text: Choose the correct preposition: 'He is interested ___ learning accounting.'
questions.explanation: The standard idiomatic expression is 'interested in'.
